title: optimize-cpu-request-path-thread-pinning-and-serialization
author: Diego Alvarez
description: Motivation: Several production incidents and perf canaries showed the CPU request path dominating tail latency in small-sequence workloads. Root cause analysis pointed to three correlated issues: (1) expensive per-request serialization/deserialization allocations, (2) contention in the global request thread pool during high-concurrency bursts, and (3) OS-level thread scheduling causing hot threads to migrate across cores, invalidating CPU caches. Summary: This PR applies a set of targeted CPU-side optimizations to reduce latency and jitter for short-sequence inference requests: 1) replace per-request std::string/json allocations with a preallocated, arena-backed serializer for common paths; 2) introduce a request-affinity thread pool that pins worker threads to CPU cores (configurable per-deployment); 3) add lightweight batching-aware scheduling to avoid thundering bursts into the kernel; 4) micro-optimizations for KV cache lookup hot paths (reduce locks and use read-mostly atomics). What changed (high level): - Add runtime/serializer/arena_serializer.{h,cpp}: small arena with fast-path write methods used by request path. - Refactor runtime/request_path.cpp to use arena serializer and to avoid temporary heap allocations in the hot loop. - Introduce runtime/threading/request_thread_pool.{h,cpp} which supports optional core pinning, per-thread batch queues, and cooperative yielding for high-utilization scenarios. - Add config options (runtime/config/threading.h) to expose pinning and pool sizes with sane defaults. - Replace a mutex-protected KV-cache lookup with a read-mostly variant using shared atomic pointers and epoch-based reclamation for entries. Checklist: - [x] Microbenchmarks for serializer and thread-pool under synthetic load - [x] End-to-end canary against perf-lab: 30% p99 latency reduction on short-seq workloads - [x] Unit tests for new thread pool and serializer - [x] Feature-flag guarded rollout for pinning to avoid regressions in noisy multi-tenant hosts Testing: Extensive unit tests included. Performance runs: perf-canary showed median improvement of ~12% and p99 improvement of ~28% for seq<=32 benchmarks. Tested on dedicated and hosted infra; thread pinning disabled by default for hosted to avoid interfering with noisy neighbors. Rollout plan: Merge behind feature flag. Gradual canary in Dedicated pools (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Monitor p95/p99 and CPU steal metrics. If CPU steal > threshold, automatically disable pinning for that pool. Notes: This PR focuses on CPU-side improvements only and does not touch GPU kernels. The KV cache changes are minimal and safe for immediate rollout; epoch reclamation is implemented conservatively to avoid ABA issues.

review_comments: Maya Patel: Can you measure the impact of arena reset frequency on long-lived requests? If reset is too aggressive we may retain larger buffers than needed.

Diego Alvarez: Answered: arena reset is tied to request boundary for short-seq fast path; long requests bypass arena and use streaming serializer to prevent unbounded retention. Added unit test for reset behavior.
Sasha Kim: The pinning API is useful, but we should avoid enabling it by default for hosted. Add a feature flag and documentation for operators.
Diego Alvarez: Added feature-flag 'thread_pinning.enabled' and documented default=false for hosted. Updated rollout notes in PR description.
Ethan Li: Concern: epoch reclamation complexity. Did we rely on hazard pointers or a simpler epoch? Also add perf test for cache lookup under concurrent writes.
Diego Alvarez: Implemented a conservative epoch recorder (single-writer cadence) and added concurrent writer microbench. Left detailed hazard pointer implementation as a follow-up (ENG-2401).
ci_checks: perf-regression-check: pass (after 3 runs, initial flaky due to CI noise)
merge_details: merge_commit_message: 'optimize(cpu): reduce request-path allocations, add thread pinning and read-mostly KV cache (ENG-2345)'
release_notes: CPU request-path optimizations: reduced allocations via arena serializer, new request-affinity thread pool with optional CPU pinning, and read-mostly KV cache lookup to lower contention. Feature-flagged pinning; disabled by default in hosted environments.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag 'thread_pinning.enabled' only after verifying host CPU steal < 2%. For Dedicated pools we recommend enabling on homogeneous, single-tenant hosts. Monitor pid-level CPU affinity and p99 latencies closely during rollout.
